originality.rationale: The claim classifies maximizers of intersection of DISTINCT standardized deletion-child sets, especially 600 labeled unordered pairs at n=8. Smith (2006) proves injectivity of entire set-valued decks, not maxima of partial overlaps; Gouveia and Lehtonen (2021) determine MULTISET-deck maximal intersections and tabulate those maximizers, not the complete maximizers for the distinct-child statistic. The 2021 n=8 multiset extremum five may imply the numeric bound four after further examination of its table, so that numerical upper bound alone is not claimed as new. Wu et al. (2026) investigate asymptotic coding and parent enumeration, not the exact finite equality classification. Source text was inspected in the relevant sections; accessible mathematical-record searches yielded no equivalent statement, but unindexed work remains possible.

value.rationale: Distinct received standardized deletion patterns are the natural observable set in permutation-invariant deletion reconstruction, distinct from the multiset deck of repeated deletion positions. At both n=7 and n=8, published multiset overlap reaches five while the set-valued extremum remains four; at n=8 the distinct-shadow equality cases form exactly 600 pairs, unlike the 16 listed multiset extrema. The complete rigid classification of all 600 worst-case set-valued collision pairs (not only their number) is a motivated finite reconstruction benchmark with a uniform local-block structural explanation. The exact classification does not pretend to solve larger n.
